articles.title: David Beckham's perfume, Poundland – and a mighty, mighty stink | Arwa Mahdawi
articles.summary: The Beckhams have made an art of monetising their every move. But apparently there are limits to where they’re prepared to sell their wares. Thoughts and half-price prayers with Poundland, please. The discount chain has been on the verge of collapse for a while, and its future looks bleak.
body: Not literally, by the way: I suppose I should spell that out since we’re dealing with a litigious billionaire. I did not mean to imply or cause a reasonable person to infer that Sir David is standing on Brixton high street kicking a Poundland. Rather, DB Ventures, the licensor of the David Beckham brand, is causing a bit of a stink about the fact that the football legend’s fragrance range was found on sale in the discount store as well as at other purveyors of budget goods. It is now suing the perfume company, Coty, which it further accuses of under reporting sales, for $41m (£31m).

“DB Ventures … ensures that all of its brand licensing partnerships maintain the lifestyle and luxury image of the brand that Sir David has carefully cultivated for decades,” court filings stated. “Imagine, then, the shock and dismay experienced when DB Ventures discovered that David Beckham products were being offered for sale in a gas station. How could this possibly have happened? Desperation and greed.” Coty has denied that it had ever sold the fragrances in Poundland.

articles.title: Get vaccinated, don’t vape – and moisturise liberally! 10 doctors on how to avoid and treat winter ailments
articles.summary: The nights are drawing in, the temperature is dropping, festive overindulgence is on the horizon and it’s easy to get run down. Here’s some expert advice to help you safely through the season.
body: Winter can be a challenging time, with bad weather, dark evenings, horrible bugs circulating, plus plenty of opportunities for overindulging. How can we avoid getting run down? Doctors share their tips for surviving the season, from saunas to screen blockers, light boxes to apples.

“I make sure I have my flu vaccine as early as I can. I had influenza B last year and it took me three months to recover. The vaccine has been shown to be more effective if you have a healthy gut microbiome, so I’ve been upping my intake of fermented foods.

“I avoid using too much ibuprofen and paracetamol if I’m ill. There is some suggestion that ibuprofen isn’t helpful to our immune system and in adults, we don’t always have to lower a fever; it may even be useful in clearing infections. I take 25 micrograms of vitamin D and omega-3 supplements but I am sceptical about other things. What I will have is small amounts of spices, such as a quarter teaspoon of turmeric, cinnamon and some ground cloves in some coconut or almond milk.

articles.title: A moment that changed me: the tomato pasta that became an obsession – and helped me lead a better life
articles.summary: At a restaurant in Italy in 2022, every forkful of my meal made my eyes close and mouth water. For four years since, I have tried to recreate this dish. The pursuit has finally made me a proper vegetarian. I’ve ostensibly been vegetarian for 13 years and, in that time, I’ve eaten a lot of meat.
body: Then I ate a bowl of pasta. It was 2022 and an Italian university friend, Mattia, invited me to Tuscany. I spent four days with his lovely family, in the rolling verdant hills, with fireflies and fallow deer keeping us company, drinking vernaccia and talking of books and art and poetry. But none of that matters, not even a bit. All that matters is a single plate of tomato pasta from Nuova Trattoria Albana, in Mazzolla, west of Siena. This pasta might have seemed, to the untrained palate, like any other pasta. But it changed everything for me.

The pici – handrolled Tuscan pasta, much thicker than spaghetti, a bit thicker than bucatini – was audaciously al dente. The pecorino, sourced from a nearby farm, melted like snow. But the sauce, all’aglione (with garlic), stole the show: the chef’s wife grew tomatoes in the garden next door, picking them fresh every day. Every forkful made my eyes close and my mouth water throughout the meal. If the great object of life is sensation, as Lord Byron suggested, then I’d never felt more alive.

From picking out the right style to managing alterations to juggling multiple options (do you really want a different dress for the ceremony and the reception? For the after-party? How many gowns does one person need?), it’s a lot—even if you’re planning a courthouse affair. We’re here to streamline the process, with our edit of the best wedding dresses you can buy online.
It starts with getting a sense of what’s out there; so to help kick off your search, we pulled together a range of wedding dresses that’ll suit every setting, dress code, and personal style.

Looking to go traditional? There’s no beating a classic, fairytale-inspired dress. These designs are built to be showstoppers, whether you opt for a bubble-skirt gown from Danielle Frankel or a style with subtle drama by Self-Portrait, Emilia Wickstead, or The OWN Studio.

articles.summary: The best places to stay in Antwerp offer a chance to adjust to the city’s quiet rhythm—whether that means finding calm in a former convent, or slowing down in a well-appointed Airbnb.
body: Winter is an especially lovely time to visit—even when it drizzles (trust me, it will), Antwerp feels delightfully festive: Christmas markets take over the Old Town square, with glowing lights strung up all over the city. The ongoing Antwerp Six exhibit at the MoMu makes a trip this holiday season particularly timely; the group’s first major retrospective closes on January 17, 2027.

Couples wishing to explore the grounds can unwind with a treatment in the spa—which includes an intimate swimming pond—then dine in the on-site restaurant. (If weather allows, try to book a table in the outdoor terrace.) While the hotel is located in one of Antwerp’s quieter neighborhoods, het Groen Kwartier, you’re still within walking distance from most of the action, including two local favorites: Bar Vert for a low-key lunch, and Funk (an essential personal bookmark) for breakfast pastries.

articles.title: The Fearless Sensitivity of ‘Mouse’ and ‘Clarissa’ Star Sophie Okonedo
articles.summary: This winter, the British actress leads two striking independent features: “Clarissa,” by brothers Chuko and Arie Esiri, and “Mouse,” by the husband-and-wife team of Kelly O’Sullivan and Alex Thompson.
body: Sophie Okonedo is one of those performers whose very presence can make a scene feel more alive. The Tony Award-winning British actress projects both warmth and watchfulness, moving swiftly from humor to hurt, or authority to vulnerability, without announcing the shift. Even in a supporting role, she has a way of making you lean in.

Filming in Lagos proved consequential in ways that extended well beyond the work itself. “The journey I had in Lagos was so immense, personally and professionally, that I remember thinking on the wrap day that even if nothing else happens with this film, I’ve already gotten everything I wanted,” she tells me.
Both films were made on tiny budgets, and, as Okonedo points out, a conversation about one inevitably opens up a conversation about the other. So, we talked about both.
Vogue: Let’s start with Mouse. How did it come to you? What was it about your character Helen, or about directors Kelly and Alex, that made you say yes?

articles.title: Caramelized Cabbage Pasta
articles.summary: The easiest way to cram an entire head of cabbage into dinner.
body: This pasta is the easiest way to cram an entire head of cabbage into one comforting dinner. The secret? Cooking it in butter over a long, relaxed period of time until it softens into a decadent, caramelized tangle. Paired with spaghetti, heavy cream, and some Dijon mustard and lemon zest to brighten everything up, this dish is a celebration of how versatile cabbage can be. Feel free to top your bowl with lots of fresh dill, or leave it unadorned with nothing more than an extra sprinkle of cheese.

Cook 12 oz. spaghetti in a large pot of boiling generously salted water, stirring occasionally, until very al dente, about 1 minute less than package directions. Drain, reserving 2 cups pasta cooking liquid. Set aside.

Melt 4 Tbsp. unsalted butter in same pot over high heat. Add 1 large head of green cabbage (about 3 lb.), cored, thinly sliced, and 6 garlic cloves, thinly sliced, and cook, stirring often, until cabbage is very tender and browned in spots, 18–25 minutes.
points: The easiest way to cram an entire head of cabbage into dinner.

articles.title: Hating Turkey Doesn’t Make You Cool
articles.summary: It’s called Turkey Day for a reason. Because it’s actually really good.
body: It is fun to be contrarian. I admit to the light thrill it gives me to tell people that I hate oat milk, or that I prefer a wet martini. It’s healthy for all of us to have our preferences. But sometimes, what should be a matter of personal taste goes viral, amassing an army of haters who make this preference their entire personality. Think back to the great cake vs pie wars of the 2010s, when anyone who admitted to liking cake was a tasteless rube. This isn’t even about what you like anymore—it’s about the attention that comes with going against the mainstream.
This is all to say that complaining about turkey on Thanksgiving has got to stop. It is good, and I need people to stop pretending as if it’s not.
